items.title: Montu Pharmacy Assessment Centre
items.snippet: Ready to start or take the next step in your pharmacy career? At Montu, we are doing things differently, and that includes how we recruit. We are growing, and we are looking for enthusiastic, hardworking and patient-focused individuals to join our pharmacy team in Winnersh Triangle. Whether you are looking to take your first step into healthcare, explore a new career in pharmacy or bring your existing pharmacy experience to a rapidly growing organisation, we would love to meet you. We are hosting a Pharmacy Assessment Centre on Saturday 5th December , giving you the opportunity to experience a different approach to recruitment, demonstrate your skills and learn more about what it is like to work at Montu. You do not need previous pharmacy experience for all of our opportunities. For our entry-level positions, what matters most is your attitude, willingness to learn and genuine commitment to making a difference to patients. Our pharmacy is busy. Really busy. It is a lively, energetic environment where things move quickly, teamwork is essential and no two days are quite the same. If you enjoy being on your feet, working alongside others and being part of a team where everyone has a role to play, you could feel right at home. Behind every prescription we process is a patient relying on us to get things right. Whether you are packing medication, dispensing prescriptions or completing final accuracy checks, your contribution matters. Opportunities Available We are recruiting across several positions within our pharmacy team, with opportunities for both experienced pharmacy professionals and individuals looking to enter the industry. Pharmacy Assistant An excellent entry point into the pharmacy sector, with no previous pharmacy experience required. You will support the day-to-day operations of our busy pharmacy, including preparing orders, packing medication, supporting stock management and helping ensure prescriptions are processed accurately and efficiently. We are looking for individuals who are organised, reliable, comfortable with repetitive tasks and enjoy working in a hands-on, fast-paced environment. Trainee Pharmacy Dispenser Looking to develop a career in pharmacy? This could be your opportunity. No previous dispensing experience is required. You will receive training and support as you develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to work within our dispensing team. You will learn about prescription processing, medication handling, accuracy, pharmacy procedures and the importance of maintaining high standards of patient safety. Pharmacy Dispenser For individuals with an existing dispensing qualification and experience working within a pharmacy environment. You will support the safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, working closely with pharmacists, technicians and the wider pharmacy team. You will need excellent attention to detail, a strong understanding of pharmacy procedures and the ability to maintain accuracy while managing high prescription volumes. Accuracy Checking Dispenser We are looking for qualified and experienced Accuracy Checking Dispensers who can help maintain the high standards of accuracy and patient safety expected within our pharmacy. You will undertake accuracy checking duties within the scope of your qualification, training and authorisation, supporting the efficient processing of prescriptions and working collaboratively with the wider team. Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT) For qualified Pharmacy Technicians with an accredited accuracy checking qualification and current GPhC registration. You will play an important role in maintaining dispensing accuracy, supporting pharmacy operations and ensuring our processes meet the required professional and regulatory standards. You will bring confidence, attention to detail and the ability to work effectively in a high-volume dispensing environment. What Is Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre? We know that traditional interviews do not always give people the best opportunity to demonstrate what they can do. That is why we are taking a slightly different approach. Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre is designed to be an engaging, practical and interactive experience where you can demonstrate your abilities, meet members of the Montu team and gain a better understanding of our working environment. You can expect a combination of practical and team-based activities designed to assess skills relevant to working within our pharmacy, including: Attention to detail and accuracy Literacy and the ability to follow written instructions Working effectively with others Organisation and the ability to follow processes Speed and efficiency without compromising accuracy Communication and problem-solving We are not expecting everyone to arrive with pharmacy knowledge, particularly those applying for our entry-level opportunities. We are interested in how you approach tasks, how you work with others and whether you have the right attitude to succeed in our environment. What happens after the assessment centre? Candidates who successfully complete the assessment centre will be invited to attend a further on-site interview at Montu on a later date. Please note that attendance at the assessment centre does not guarantee an interview or offer of employment. What Are We Looking For? We are looking for people who genuinely want to be part of a team making a difference. Our ideal candidates will be: Patient-focused: You understand that the work you do has a direct impact on the people relying on our service. Detail-oriented: Accuracy matters, particularly when working with medication. Comfortable in a busy environment: You enjoy an energetic workplace and can remain focused when things get hectic. Reliable and hardworking: You take pride in doing your job well and supporting the people around you. Team players: You understand that pharmacy operations depend on people working together. Adaptable: You are comfortable learning new processes and responding to change. Eager to learn: Whether you are new to pharmacy or already experienced, you are motivated to develop your skills. You do not need to be the loudest person in the room or have years of experience to succeed here. What matters is your work ethic, your attention to detail and your commitment to doing things properly. About Montu Montu is a leading medical cannabis company working to improve access to cannabis-based medicines for patients across the UK. Through our specialist clinical services and pharmacy operations, we support patients receiving prescribed cannabis-based medicines for a range of eligible medical conditions. Our multidisciplinary teams bring together clinicians, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, dispensers and operational colleagues, all working towards the same goal: delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care. We are a rapidly growing organisation, and our pharmacy is at the heart of what we do. Every prescription represents a patient who is depending on us. From the moment a prescription reaches our pharmacy to the moment medication is dispatched, every member of our team plays an important role in that patient journey. We are proud to be helping shape an evolving area of healthcare, and we want people who are excited to be part of that journey. Why Join Montu? Joining Montu means becoming part of a growing organisation where your work has purpose and your contribution makes a difference. We offer: Competitive salaries dependent on the position, qualifications and experience Opportunities for training and professional development Career progression within our growing pharmacy operations A supportive and collaborative team environment The opportunity to gain experience within a specialist area of healthcare The chance to be part of a growing business helping improve patient access to prescribed medication Further information about the benefits applicable to each role will be provided during the recruitment process. Ready to Join Us? Assessment Centre: Saturday 5th December Location: Winnersh Triangle, Berkshire If you are looking for an opportunity to begin a career in pharmacy, develop your existing skills or take the next step within a growing healthcare organisation, we would love to hear from you. Apply now to be considered for a place at our Pharmacy Assessment Centre. Following an initial review of applications, shortlisted candidates will receive further information about the assessment centre, including timings, location details and what to expect on the day. items.title: AI and Digital Solutions Engineer
items.snippet: Department / Business Unit Baines Simmons /Operations Reports To Operations Director Direct Reports None Grade / Band Graduate Location UK Hybrid (Bracknell) Employment Type Full-time Budget Responsibility None Purpose of the Role TrustFlight’s Operations department delivers a high volume of aviation safety training, consultancy, and compliance services to clients globally. As the business scales, the administrative and coordination burden across scheduling, travel, contracting, and client communications has grown significantly. This role exists to identify, design, and implement digital and AI-powered solutions that automate and streamline the operational workflows underpinning consultant scheduling, travel logistics, contractor management, and client-facing communications — including course joining instructions, certificates, course materials, and Microsoft Teams setup. The AI & Digital Solutions Engineer will act as the bridge between operational need and technology capability, transforming manual, repetitive processes into scalable, intelligent workflows that free the wider team to focus on high-value delivery. Whilst Operations is the primary focus, the role will also extend AI and automation capability into Business Development and Product, supporting pipeline workflows, proposal generation, and product feedback processes as the function matures. Scope & Decision-Making Authority Design, build, and deploy automation solutions for agreed operational workflows using AI and no-code/low-code tooling, within a structured support framework during the initial onboarding period. Select and recommend appropriate tools and platforms for workflow automation, within agreed budget parameters and subject to IT governance sign-off. Propose and pilot new digital solutions with line manager oversight, progressing toward greater autonomy as experience and confidence develop. Escalate to Operations Director for significant new vendor contracts, material changes to client-facing communications, or solutions that touch personal or sensitive data. Cross-functional coordination with Training Delivery, Consulting, Client Success, Business Development, and Product teams to gather requirements and implement agreed solutions. Scope covers Operations as the primary function, with cross-functional remit extending to Business Development and Product from day one. Key Relationships Internal Operations Director — regular check-in on priorities, solution sign-off, and strategic alignment. Operations Coordinators, Admins & Consultants — day-to-day requirements gathering, testing, and adoption support for new workflows. IT & Engineering — technical governance, data security review, and integration support where required. Senior Leadership Team — periodic reporting on operational efficiency gains and automation ROI. Business Development Team — automation of proposal generation, CRM workflows, and pipeline reporting. Product Team — digital tooling support for product feedback loops, release communications, and internal reporting. External Training & Consultancy Clients — automated and semi-automated communications for joining instructions, certificates, course materials, and Teams invitations. Contractors & Freelance Consultants — digital onboarding, contracting, scheduling notifications, and engagement management. Software & Platform Vendors — procurement, configuration, and ongoing management of automation and scheduling tools. Key Responsibilities Audit and map current operational workflows — including consultant scheduling, travel booking, contractor contracting, and client communications — to identify automation and AI opportunities. Design and build end-to-end digital workflows using AI tools, automation platforms, and scheduling systems to reduce manual effort across the Operations team. Implement intelligent scheduling solutions for consultant time allocation, ensuring visibility of availability, conflict resolution, and automated notifications to all parties. Automate the full client communication lifecycle for training and consultancy engagements, including generation and dispatch of joining instructions, course materials, Teams meeting invitations, and post-course certificates. Build and maintain a digital contractor management workflow covering sourcing triggers, contract generation, engagement tracking, and payment milestone coordination. Own the technology stack for Operations automation — evaluating tools, managing licences, and ensuring solutions remain fit for purpose as the business evolves. Champion adoption of new digital workflows across the Operations team, providing training, documentation, and ongoing support. Monitor solution performance, identify failure points, and continuously improve automations to increase reliability and coverage. Support the Business Development team with AI-assisted proposal workflows, CRM automation, and pipeline visibility tooling to accelerate the sales cycle. Collaborate with the Product team to design and implement digital solutions that streamline product feedback collection, internal reporting, and release communication processes. Key Metrics for Success Within 90 days: Full audit of operational workflows completed and an automation roadmap agreed with the Operations Director. Within 6 months: At least 3 core workflows automated (e.g. consultant scheduling notifications, client joining instructions, contractor contract generation), with measurable reduction in manual processing time of ≥40%. Within 12 months: End-to-end automation coverage across scheduling, travel coordination triggers, client communications, and contractor onboarding, delivering a quantified saving of ≥60 hours/week for the Operations team. Client communication error rate (wrong materials, missed invites, late certificates) reduced to <1% of engagements. Stakeholder satisfaction score of 4+/5 from internal Operations team on quality and usability of implemented solutions. Deliver at least one agreed automation solution for each of Business Development and Product within the first 12 months. AI & Digital Competency TrustFlight is an AI-first organisation. Every role is expected to actively engage with AI tools and digital ways of working to drive efficiency, quality, and innovation. AI Fluency Tier Tier Profile Expectations Tier 3 — AI Builder ✓ Develops and integrates AI-powered solutions Builds, fine-tunes, or integrates AI/ML models and pipelines. Establishes evaluation frameworks for AI systems. Ensures responsible AI practices (fairness, transparency, data governance). Contributes to TrustFlight’s AI strategy. Role-Specific AI & Digital Skills Design and deploy AI-assisted scheduling systems that intelligently match consultant availability to client demand, accounting for skills, location, and travel constraints. Use LLM-powered tools to auto-generate personalised client communications — joining instructions, Teams invites, course materials packs, and post-course certificates. Build AI-assisted contractor matching and contract generation workflows, reducing turnaround time from requirement to signed agreement. Apply AI tools for document classification and routing — ensuring the right materials reach the right clients at the right time. Leverage AI-powered analytics to surface operational bottlenecks and recommend process improvements proactively. AI Development & Growth Complete TrustFlight’s AI fluency onboarding programme within first 30 days. Share automation wins, prompt libraries, and AI use cases with the wider team on a quarterly basis. Actively participate in TrustFlight’s internal AI community of practice, contributing Operations-specific use cases and learnings. Competencies & Behaviours Innovation — Proactively identifies and implements technology-driven improvements; comfortable experimenting with new tools and approaches. Delivery Focus — Takes ownership of solutions end-to-end; balances speed of iteration with stability and reliability of outputs. Collaboration — Builds trust with non-technical stakeholders; listens carefully to operational needs before designing solutions. Customer Centricity — Keeps the client experience and consultant wellbeing central to every workflow decision. Analytical Thinking — Breaks down complex, multi-step processes into logical components; uses data to prioritise and validate improvements. Adaptability — Thrives in a fast-moving environment; adjusts priorities readily as operational needs evolve. Working Arrangements Working Hours 37.5 hours per week, core hours 09:00–17:00 Work Pattern Hybrid — minimum 3 days office (Bracknell) for first 6 months, 2–3 days thereafter Travel Requirements None Anticipated On-Call / Shift Work None Special Conditions Right to work in the UK required Required Qualifications & Experience A degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a closely related technical discipline — achieved or expected at 2:1 or above. Demonstrated academic study of AI and machine learning concepts, including LLMs, automation, or intelligent systems — evidenced through coursework, dissertations, modules, or equivalent self-directed learning. Ability to demonstrate understanding of how AI tools can be applied to real-world process automation, through academic projects, coursework examples, or personal study. Familiarity with at least one automation or no-code/low-code platform (e.g. Make, Power Automate, n8n, Zapier) — whether through university projects, personal experimentation, or placement experience. Comfortable working analytically with data and processes — able to break down a workflow logically and identify where technology can add value. Strong communication skills — able to translate technical concepts for non-technical colleagues and listen carefully before designing solutions. Organised, reliable, and able to manage competing priorities — follows through on commitments and flags issues early. Desirable Skills & Experience Placement year, internship, or part-time experience in a technology, operations, or business environment. Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs (e.g. Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT) in a project or academic context. Familiarity with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, particularly Teams, as a communications and workflow platform. Exposure to APIs, webhooks, or data integration between SaaS platforms. Experience with document generation tools or CRM platforms. Awareness of UK GDPR and data privacy considerations as they apply to automated communications and personal data. Interest in or knowledge of aviation, professional services, or regulated industries. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

items.title: Junior Video Editor & Camera Operator
items.snippet: About Tessl AI is transforming how software is built, and at Tessl, we're building the infrastructure for what comes next. We're developing a platform that enables engineering teams to build and run AI-powered software factories, where coding agents take on real development work, from picking up engineering tickets to implementing changes and creating pull requests. By combining structured context, reusable agent skills, automated workflows and evaluations, we're making AI-powered development more reliable, repeatable and scalable, while keeping humans in control. We're tackling some of the biggest challenges in autonomous software development, from code quality and security to helping organisations confidently adopt AI agents at scale. Founded by Guy Podjarny, previously founder of Snyk, Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup backed by over $100 million in funding from investors including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart. Joining Tessl means helping define an entirely new category of technology, solving ambitious technical challenges and shaping the future of software development. About the role We're hiring a junior video editor and camera operator to help make everything Tessl puts on camera: The AI Native Dev podcast, product videos, webinars, livestreams and our AI DevCon conferences. You'll work hand in hand with our video producer (Tom Dowler) in the Marketing team, shooting alongside him and owning a growing share of the edit and publishing. This is an entry-level role. We care more about curiosity, drive and a willingness to pitch in than a polished portfolio, but you'll need to show you can already shoot and cut a decent piece of video. What you'll do Shoot. Assist on every shoot: podcast recordings, product videos, webinars, livestreams and full conference days. Rig cameras, lights and audio, operate a camera, and manage media on set. Cut the podcast. Deliver first-pass edits of AI Native Dev episodes, ready for review. Make social cuts. Turn long edits into short clips built for YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels. Finish the picture and sound. Edit, color correct and grade, edit and mix audio, pick music and create captions. Publish. Schedule finished episodes and videos to podcast platforms, YouTube and our social channels. Automate the boring parts. Use and extend our AI-assisted post-production pipeline (transcripts, captions, clip finding, publishing assets), and build your own automations wherever you spot repetitive work. What you'll bring Proof you can shoot and cut. A short reel, a few clips, a YouTube channel or a uni project that shows basic competence behind the camera and in the edit. Camera range. You're comfortable shooting on a wide range of cameras, and you know your way around lighting and sound on set. The software stack. You're comfortable in Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Photoshop and Audition, DaVinci Resolve and Figma. A pro-AI attitude. You already use AI tools in your work, and you're comfortable building and running AI automations to speed up your own workflow. Curiosity and drive. You ask good questions, pick things up fast and pitch in wherever you're needed, from carrying flight cases to cutting a trailer. Some experience. Around 1 to 2 years in production or editing (in a job, freelance or self-taught) is typical for this role, but it isn't a hard requirement. Nice to have The Blackmagic ecosystem, in depth. Cinema cameras, ATEM switchers, HyperDeck recorders and Blackmagic RAW workflows through to Resolve. Live production. Vision mixing, multicam recording or running a livestream. Motion graphics. Titles, lower thirds and simple animation in After Effects. Curiosity about software and AI. You'll be filming developers talking about AI coding agents every week, so it helps if you want to understand what they're saying. Application Process Send us three things. A polished portfolio isn't required. Your CV. A link to 2 to 5 minutes of your work (a reel, YouTube, Vimeo or a Drive folder), with a line on what you shot and what you edited. A few sentences on one AI tool or automation you use in your video work, and what it saves you. Life at Tessl We want Tessl to be a place where you can do meaningful work, keep learning and enjoy being part of the team. Alongside competitive compensation, we offer benefits designed to support you both inside and outside work. What we offer Competitive compensation and equity: Market-benchmarked salaries and EMI share options. Time off: 25 days of annual leave, plus UK public holidays, and two paid volunteering days each year. Private healthcare: Vitality medical insurance, including dental, optical and mental health support, with cover included for partners and dependants. Pension: A 5% employer pension matched contribution through Smart Pension. Life assurance: Company-paid life insurance with MetLife providing cover of four times your annual salary. Family Leave: We offer enhanced Maternity, Parental and Adoption Leave from day one to support you and your growing family. Learning and development: We support opportunities to continue developing your skills with a £1,000 per year to spend. Commuting benefits: Financial support for eligible team members commuting from outside Greater London, plus a Cycle to Work scheme. Summer & winter offsites: Twice a year, we bring the whole Tessl team together for a week-long offsite. It's a chance to step away from our usual routines, collaborate on big ideas, build stronger relationships and enjoy shared experiences together. And of course, we have a lot of fun along the way! Our London HQ Our office is in the heart of King's Cross, surrounded by London's growing AI and technology community. We work together in person on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, giving us time to collaborate, exchange ideas and build relationships. You'll also enjoy catered lunches (Tuesday & Thursday), plenty of office snacks, regular team lunches and socials, plus a pet-friendly workplace. How we work Our operating principles shape how we collaborate and make decisions. We move quickly and learn by doing, build on ideas before challenging them, get stuck in wherever we can help, and give people real ownership. We encourage thoughtful debate, curiosity and a willingness to try things that haven't been done before. Read our five operating principles . We're AI native AI isn't just what we're building - it's central to how we work every day, across every function. We actively use AI to improve how we work, solve problems and challenge traditional ways of doing things. You don't need to be an AI expert to thrive at Tessl, but you do need curiosity, an appetite for experimentation and a willingness to embrace new ways of working. We expect everyone to use AI regularly, invest time in learning how to get the most from it and keep experimenting when something doesn't work the first time, rather than defaulting to manual approaches. We're also big believers in sharing what we learn. We encourage transparency about how we're using AI, what's working, what isn't and how we can help each other improve. Being AI native doesn't mean removing human judgement, it means using AI thoughtfully, while taking ownership of the quality and outcomes of our work. Everyone is welcome at Tessl We're committed to building an inclusive environment where people from different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives can thrive. We particularly welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in technology. If you're excited about the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still encourage you to apply. If you need any adjustments or additional support during the recruitment process, please let us know. We're happy to work with you to make the process accessible and comfortable. Come build with us We're moving fast, experimenting boldly and figuring things out as we go. There's plenty to build, lots to learn and real opportunities to make your mark. If you're excited by big ideas, enjoy getting stuck in and want to be part of something from the ground up, we'd love to hear from you! Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

As we expand our reach globally, Dandy is building the operating system for dental offices around the world—empowering clinicians and their teams with technology, innovation, and world-class support to achieve more for their practices, their people, and their patients. Backed by some of the world's leading venture capital firms, we're on an ambitious mission to simplify and modernise every function of the dental practice through technology. As we expand internationally, Dandy is building the operating system for dental practices around the world, empowering clinicians and their teams with technology, innovation and world-class support to achieve more for their practices, their people and their patients. items.snippet: Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented. The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code. We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched. We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe. The Role You generate pipeline for our account executives (AEs) in the markets where dollar access is hardest. Most of it happens in person, at conferences and the events around them. In between, you find the next targets and make sure every lead lands with the right AE. You also own the numbers behind the top of the funnel and use them to recommend where the team spends its time next, including which new markets are worth testing. You'll help shape how we run Growth, with real autonomy and a scope that grows with what you show. Your First Six Months Months 1-2: Learn the product, our ICP and how we sell to banks and fintechs. Shadow our sales conversations, and get to know our stack, our playbooks and the way we operate. Go to your first conference with the team: help with pre-booking, work the floor alongside our Sales and Growth teams, and book your first meetings. By the end of month two, you can pitch Augustus on your own. Months 3-4: Execution is yours. Own a conference end to end, from the target list to the follow-up: book the meetings, route each one to the right AE and make sure it happens. Take meetings on your own and work closely with Sales and Marketing. Months 5-6: Own the pipeline for a set of markets and run your first event. You've turned what you've learned into data: which conferences, intros and markets bring deals that close, and which don't. You sync with the rest of GTM to bring in what they see and use it to shape our market strategy: where we go next, how we go in, who we target first and what we lead with. Who Will Thrive At Augustus We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits: American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low. Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment. Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team. Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent. This role is for you if: You're outgoing and at your best in front of people. You can start a conversation with a stranger at a booth and hold it with a bank's CFO. You do what needs to be done, even when it's not glamorous: building a prospecting list, chasing a follow-up, carrying boxes to the booth. You think clearly and work from data. You take an unstructured dataset and come back with answers and insights. You're diligent and organised. Nothing falls through the cracks. You use AI to move fast, but don't trust the output blindly. You check results, question the systems and don't ship anything you wouldn't put your name on. You're curious: when something takes too long, you find a faster way to do it. After every conference, you know what you'd do differently next time, and you do it. This is not for you if: You'd rather work behind a screen than in front of people. Most of our pipeline starts with a conversation in person. You want a well-defined scope and clear processes. Ours change as we grow, and you'll help build many of them. You want a predictable week. Plans change, the bar is high and the hours are long. You expect your degree to count for more than your results. You have 1-2 previous internships or roles in high-growth startups, venture capital, private equity, consulting or investment banking, and/or you have demonstrated initiative through side projects, student organizations or entrepreneurial experiences. Fluent English. Spanish is a strong plus. You can travel regularly, often at short notice. Based in Berlin or willing to relocate. Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities. Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.
